title: Which Settlement a Third Party's Compensation Answers
content:
Which settlement on a policy of the Travel Protection Plans a third party's compensation answers is read
off two records together: the policy's own claim record, and the carrier's ledger of the traveller's air
bookings held under the Air Ticket Fare Brands, whose payout lines carry the ground each was raised on.

## The three readings

| What the two records show | The settlement the compensation answers |
|---|---|
| The carrier's ledger carries a payout raised on an involuntary schedule change, and the claim record carries a payment made on a missed connection | The payment made on the missed connection head |
| The carrier's ledger carries no payout raised on an involuntary schedule change, and the claim record carries a payment made on a travel delay | The payment made on the travel delay head |
| Neither of those holds | The payment standing last on the policy's claim record |

Each reading is a compound condition, and both of its parts must hold: a schedule-change payout on the carrier's
side without a missed connection payment on the claim record does not reach the first reading, and a travel
delay payment on the claim record does not reach the second while any schedule-change payout stands on the
carrier's ledger.

## Points of judgement

Where the claim record carries payments on both a missed connection and a travel delay, and the carrier's ledger
carries a payout raised on an involuntary schedule change, the missed connection payment is the settlement
answered — the first reading holds, and the second is closed by the presence of the schedule-change payout.
Where the same claim record stands but the carrier's ledger carries only payouts raised on an airline
cancellation, the second reading holds instead and the travel delay payment is the settlement answered. Where
the claim record carries neither head, the payment standing last on it is the settlement answered, whatever the
carrier's ledger shows.
